findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-measure the Bedrock IAM precondition against current infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf (line 20 already grants InvokeModel on amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0) and correct the plan: if the ADR picks Titan the embedding ARN is already present and verifiable per bedrock-access.md §4, so the 'named gating prerequisite' applies only to a model that is neither Claude nor Titan.
evidence: Plan quote: 'infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:16-17 scopes bedrock:InvokeModel to anthropic.claude-* and infra/ holds no embedding ARN, so selecting a non-Claude model (e.g. Titan) makes adding that ARN a named gating prerequisite'

infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:20 — resources already include 'arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0' inside the bedrock:InvokeModel / InvokeModelWithResponseStream statement (lines 13-21); the file header comment even says it lists 'the Titan model it embeds with'

infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md:139-159 — documents a boto3 invoke_model probe for amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 from the rebar-gerrit-instance-role, expecting EMBED_OK: 1024, confirming the grant is live (VERIFIED, not UNVERIFIED)
Evidence class: Titan embedding integration = Verified (observed in Terraform source + documented runtime probe); the plan's 'no embedding ARN' precondition = Contradicted
findings.finding: The plan's stated Bedrock precondition is contradicted by live infra: it claims iam_s7.tf scopes InvokeModel to anthropic.claude-* and that infra/ holds no embedding ARN, but the current iam_s7.tf already grants bedrock:InvokeModel on amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0, and bedrock-access.md documents a working invoke_model verification for it from the production role.
findings.location: Plan section 'Constraints every design must satisfy', bullet 'The ADR's embedding model must be callable from the production Bedrock role'
scenarios: ADR selects Titan Text Embeddings V2 and the index-and-surfacing child treats 'add the embedding ARN' as an open gating prerequisite that is in fact already satisfied, or adds a redundant/conflicting Terraform resource
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the assertion with: 'iam_s7.tf already scopes bedrock:InvokeModel to anthropic.claude-* AND amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 (verified live via bedrock-access.md §4). If the ADR selects Titan, no new ARN is needed. Only a model outside {Claude, Titan} makes adding its foundation-model ARN a named gating prerequisite before AC2/AC4 can pass in production.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define (or point AC5 at an ADR section that defines) the overlap judge's output vocabulary and decision rule — the verdict/disposition values it emits (e.g. duplicate / supersedes / related-but-distinct / abstain), the both-orderings + required-shared-artifact rule, and the default-when-unsure — rather than specifying only the ≤-2-call budget.
evidence: AC5: 'Plan review surfaces overlap findings against the same index on demand with a bounded judge budget (at most 10 candidates, at most 2 LLM calls). Checked by: the plan-review sidecar test asserting the call count.' — the check pins only the call count, not the verdict vocabulary.

Constraints bullet: 'an LLM judge runs only on demand over at most 10 lexical-or-vector candidates' — names the judge surface and its budget but no output contract (what a finding IS: duplicate / supersedes / related-but-distinct / abstain) or decision rule.

ADR 0086 (retired v1, docs/adr/0086-cross-ticket-overlap.md:75-76) DID specify the judge contract: 'pairwise judge (both orderings, a required cited shared artifact, default related-but-distinct, abstain-when-unsure)'; this plan does not reference or reuse it.
ADR 0122 (the AC1 deliverable) is scoped to retrieval; search for 'overlap' returns only a context reference, so the judge's output contract is fixed by neither AC1 nor an existing artifact.
findings.finding: The AC5 plan-review overlap LLM judge is referenced as a structured-output surface (it 'surfaces overlap findings' under a bounded budget) but its verdict vocabulary and decision rule are never defined in the plan, nor pointed at a defining artifact — unlike the retrieval architecture, which AC1's ADR fixes. The retired v1 (ADR 0086) defined exactly this contract ('pairwise judge, both orderings, a required cited shared artifact, default related-but-distinct, abstain-when-unsure'); the replacement does not carry it forward, and ADR 0122 is scoped to retrieval only.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC5 / 'Constraints every design must satisfy' bullet on bounded model calls / Child decomposition 'Plan-review overlap on demand'
scenarios: The 'Plan-review overlap on demand' child is planned: the executor must decide what verdict labels the judge emits, whether it abstains, and whether suggestions default to related-but-distinct — with no grounded vocabulary, the two LLM calls' output shape is invented ad hoc.
A plan-review sidecar consumer must render the judge's findings but the plan gives no enum of disposition values to switch on.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC5 (or the 'Constraints' judge bullet), state that the ADR records the judge's verdict enum and decision rule, carrying forward ADR 0086's specification ('both orderings, a required cited shared artifact, default related-but-distinct, abstain-when-unsure') or explicitly superseding it, and extend the AC5 check to assert the emitted disposition vocabulary in addition to the call count.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make c670's ADR freshness-key/catch-up specification and 4e89's index-and-catch-up design name the SAME key and the SAME catch-up mechanism (and align both with the parent's HEAD-SHA+format-version / git-diff-incremental constraint, or amend the parent).
evidence: c670 Approach: '... the freshness key, catch-up rule ... keyed by tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version, rebuilt on mismatch), the catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>)'.
4e89 Child decomposition: 'Lexical index and catch-up — the FTS5 index, the persisted ticket-dir to dir-hash map, enumeration-based catch-up, ranking, and the degradation paths.'
Parent constraint: 'keyed by the tickets-branch HEAD SHA and a format version ... reconciled by an incremental update over only the tickets git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head> names.'
Parent AC4: 'The ADR (AC1) fixes the concrete mechanism and its cost.'
container pairing: parent + 4e89-30b9-1666-4e53/a350-2e7e-71eb-4f5b/c670-c285-a0f9-4b40
findings.finding: The design-record child c670 and the implementation child 4e89 specify DIFFERENT freshness keys and catch-up mechanisms for the same index. c670's plan has the ADR record the freshness key as 'tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version' with catch-up as 'reader-process incremental update from git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>' (the parent's constraint), while 4e89 builds 'the persisted ticket-dir to dir-hash map, enumeration-based catch-up'. The ADR c670 produces is the binding evidence 4e89 must implement, so the two children contradict on the mechanism the parent (AC1/AC4) requires the ADR to fix.
findings.location: child c670-c285-a0f9-4b40 (Approach: freshness key + catch-up rule recorded in the ADR) vs child 4e89-30b9-1666-4e53 (Child decomposition: 'the persisted ticket-dir to dir-hash map, enumeration-based catch-up')
scenarios: An executor of 4e89 reads ADR 0122 (produced by c670) expecting a HEAD-SHA/format-version key with git-diff incremental catch-up, but 4e89's plan directs a dir-hash map with enumeration-based catch-up — the two cannot both be 'the' mechanism the ADR fixes.
The parent's two-trigger design (format-version mismatch -> full rebuild; HEAD-SHA advance -> git-diff incremental) is not what either the dir-hash/enumeration path or the measured ADR implements.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve to one mechanism: state in c670's ADR and 4e89's decomposition the identical freshness key and catch-up rule, and reconcile with the parent constraint before sign-off.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make c670's ADR-recorded index path match the path a350 (and 4e89) use for the shared index, so all children name one index location.
evidence: c670 Approach: '... the index location (<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite, keyed by tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version, rebuilt on mismatch)'.
a350 Approach: 'The sibling story builds a lexical FTS5 index under .rebar/cache/similar-tickets/, caught up in the read phase.'
Parent constraint requires derived data 'outside the replicated store'; the two paths (.git/rebar vs .rebar/cache) are different locations, only one of which either child names.
container pairing: parent + 4e89-30b9-1666-4e53/a350-2e7e-71eb-4f5b/c670-c285-a0f9-4b40
findings.finding: Children c670 and a350 record DIFFERENT index locations. c670's plan has the ADR record the index path as '<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite', while a350's plan states the sibling index lives under '.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/'. These are distinct locations for the one index both children (and 4e89) depend on.
findings.location: child c670-c285-a0f9-4b40 (Approach: 'the index location (<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite ...)') vs child a350-2e7e-71eb-4f5b (Approach: 'builds a lexical FTS5 index under .rebar/cache/similar-tickets/')
scenarios: a350's overlap feature reads find_similar expecting the index at .rebar/cache/similar-tickets/, but ADR 0122 (per c670's plan) records .git/rebar/similar.sqlite — a reader keyed to the ADR's path would not find the index a350 relies on.
Documentation/ops referencing the ADR-recorded path points at a location the implementation does not use.
findings.suggested_fix: Settle on a single path (e.g. .rebar/cache/similar-tickets/) and have c670's ADR specification, 4e89's index child, and a350's overlap child all cite that same path.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the minimum-title-length threshold (or explicitly defer it to the ADR as a tunable with a stated default, e.g. >= N characters).
evidence: Constraint: 'Compose-time suggestion is non-blocking, capped (3 to 5 results), and gated on a minimum title length.'
No minimum length (chars/words) is given anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The 'minimum title length' gate for compose-time suggestion is referenced in the constraints and implied by AC2 but no threshold value or default is stated.
findings.location: Constraints ('gated on a minimum title length'); AC2
scenarios: Implementer of the index-and-surfacing child must pick a threshold with no guidance, risking too-short-title noise or over-suppression.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a default such as 'minimum title length = 15 characters, finalized in the ADR' to the constraint and AC2.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Context claim that AC2 'must beat' the same-title baseline with the ACs — either point the recall comparison at AC1 explicitly or add the comparison to AC2.
evidence: Context: '... it now gates only the advisory create-time same-title journal, which is the baseline AC2 must beat.'
AC2 verify: 'the interface parity tests plus a timing test that asserts the store size' — no recall/quality assertion.
AC1 holds the per-stratum recall@5/recall@10 measurement.
findings.finding: The Context asserts the create-time same-title journal 'is the baseline AC2 must beat', but AC2 as written contains only a latency (p95 500ms) and interface-parity bar with no recall/quality comparison against that baseline; the quality bar actually lives in AC1.
findings.location: Context ('the baseline AC2 must beat'); AC2; AC1
scenarios: A reader expects AC2 to encode the beat-the-baseline bar and finds none, or an implementer looks to AC2 for the quality gate that is really in AC1.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Context phrasing to 'which is the baseline the AC1 semantic-stratum recall must beat' so the quality bar maps to the AC that actually measures recall.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC2: either amend the parent to the relative bound 4e89 adopts, or have 4e89 assert the parent's absolute 500 ms warm p95 (naming the host/hardware the 500 ms is defined against).
evidence: Parent AC2: '... within a p95 of 500 ms on a synthetic store at or above live size ... when the index is warm.'

Child 4e89 AC: 'Warm-index retrieval holds a p95 below the cold-catch-up p95 divided by the recorded warm-to-cold ratio ... Relative, not an absolute 500 ms: ADR 0122 records that bar at 107 ms locally but 545 ms on macos-latest.'
No sibling re-asserts the absolute 500 ms p95; the roster shows only 4e89 addressing warm-index timing.
container pairing: parent + 4e89-30b9-1666-4e53/a350-2e7e-71eb-4f5b/c670-c285-a0f9-4b40
findings.finding: Child 4e89 reinterprets parent AC2's absolute 'p95 of 500 ms (warm index)' as a RELATIVE bound ('a p95 below the cold-catch-up p95 divided by the recorded warm-to-cold ratio'), and explicitly abandons 500 ms, noting the measured warm p95 is 545 ms on macos-latest — above the parent's 500 ms. The observable outcome and the measurable terms differ, so the parent criterion is only partially covered.
findings.location: child 4e89-30b9-1666-4e53 (AC: 'Warm-index retrieval holds a p95 below the cold-catch-up p95 divided by the recorded warm-to-cold ratio ... Relative, not an absolute 500 ms')
scenarios: A completion verifier checking parent AC2 ('within a p95 of 500 ms') against 4e89's relative timing test finds the 500 ms figure is never asserted and the recorded warm p95 (545 ms) exceeds it.
Production on slower hardware passes 4e89's relative test while violating the parent's 500 ms bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one bound for both: if the relative ratio is the intended contract, amend the parent AC2 to state it (and drop the 500 ms); otherwise make 4e89 assert p95 <= 500 ms on a named reference host at >=10,000 tickets.
